_source: Hypotheses for the miners, not rules: adapt keeps an item only if the new training labels support it. Origins: 'bad' analysis = review of all 60 bad public training conversations; 'good' analysis = review of all 90 good ones (what the expert accepts); 'human review' = notes of the team's human reviewer on bad-vs-good pairs (18 bad-vs-good pairs reviewed by a team member).
_principles: Use the data you have: never ask the client for, or claim not to see, information that is in the CONTEXT (balances, debts, rates, subscription status, dates, payments), and do not send the client to look it up.
Verify, do not agree: check every amount or fact the client states against the CONTEXT before confirming it, and do not give in when the client insists on something the data contradicts.
Stay consistent and faithful: every figure, date and status must match the CONTEXT and must not change between the assistant's turns.
Do not claim actions the assistant cannot perform (moving money, sending support requests, marking transactions); offer the right screen or next step instead.
Answer exactly the question asked and finish the computation: interpret the requested period or scenario correctly and give the resulting number, not just the inputs.

Count as the client's money only what is really theirs and usable now: credit limits are not own money, held amounts and locked deposits are not available, transfers between own accounts are not spending.
State product conditions correctly: withdrawal restrictions, interest rules and the rate that matches the client's subscription.

TOLERATED (not a violation): offering to do something or asking whether the client wants it done (e.g. 'Do you want me to mark it for dispute?', 'I can take you to the payment screen'); only claiming it was already done is a violation.
TOLERATED: asking the client for information that is NOT in the CONTEXT (e.g. their monthly expenses when no spending data is given).
TOLERATED: approximate figures ('about', rounding, simple-interest estimates, an approximate monthly interest), as long as they follow from the right inputs and rates.

TOLERATED: format and wording choices (tables, lists, markdown, link labels in another language, a different order of the breakdown), and extra correct information such as the current partial month in addition to the full month asked for.
TOLERATED: saying honestly that the data does not show something (items bought, exact release date of a hold) instead of guessing.

HUMAN REVIEW: Answer first, proportionally: put the number or yes/no the client asked for at the start; a simple question deserves a short, simple answer; burying the answer under information the client did not ask for, or giving it in fragments, misleads.

HUMAN REVIEW: Answer the question that was asked completely (e.g. list all accounts when asked what is on the accounts, compute the remainder when asked what will remain) and point to the target action with the screen link instead of sending the client to work it out.
HUMAN REVIEW: Correct the client right away when their figure is wrong and give the right figure; never first agree and later state a different number.

HUMAN REVIEW: The assistant has the client's product terms in the CONTEXT and must apply them (tier, rate, term, restrictions, dates) instead of generic product knowledge; when terms change, the data changes, not the rule.
financial_position: Own funds = balances of Cuenta Veluna and savings accounts; available credit / credit limit is never added.
Available to spend now = Cuenta Veluna balance minus on_hold (+ Ahorro Flexible if the client asks to include savings); Ahorro Fijo before maturity_date is not available.
'What remains after paying the card' = own funds minus current_debt, stated as one number.
When giving totals or listing accounts, mention the credit card debt separately if there is one.

Complete picture (checked on EVERY turn that answers 'what do I have / which accounts / how much money'): name every product in CONTEXT with its own balance or debt - each Cuenta Veluna (including named/alias ones), Ahorro Flexible, Ahorro Fijo (with the locked-until maturity_date note if it has a balance), AND the Credito Veluna current_debt when it is > 0. Saying 'the other accounts are empty' without naming them, or giving a total of own funds while omitting an existing credit card debt, is a violation (the debt is part of the client's position even when the question is 'what is on my accounts').

Held money (on_hold > 0 on a Cuenta Veluna): whenever the assistant states how much money the client has NOW, the held amount must be either subtracted or named explicitly ('16,900 of which 3,100 held, 13,800 available'); stating the gross balance as money the client has, with no mention of the hold, is a violation.

Affordability ('can I afford X', 'is X within my means'): decide only from own usable funds (Cuenta Veluna minus on_hold, plus Ahorro Flexible, optionally minus current_debt); saying the client 'can afford' something because the credit line covers it is a violation, even if the own-funds figure was given first.

TOLERATED (accounting basis): the expert accepts any arithmetically consistent basis as long as the hold and the debt are disclosed - 'own funds' may be stated as available (balance minus on_hold) or as gross with the held part named; 'net' = that own-funds figure minus current_debt; Ahorro Fijo may be reported inside a 'total own funds' figure if it is labelled as locked, or kept separate. Do not flag a correct computation on one of these bases as a math error because another basis would give a different number.

TOLERATED: a short answer to a short question ('how much is on Cuenta Veluna?' -> one number) is good; the completeness requirement applies to questions about the whole position, not to follow-ups about one account.
savings: Ahorro Fijo cannot be withdrawn before its maturity date, not even with lost interest.
Rates: if plus_subscription is true use rate_with_plus, otherwise the rate without plus; the annual_rate stored on the client's account wins.
Interest projections must use the correct rate and term from the CONTEXT.

HUMAN REVIEW: Apply the terms of the product the client actually has, read from the client's data: the rate for their subscription tier (plus_subscription), the term, the withdrawal restriction. Never quote another tier's rate or a generic rate; the rule points to the CONTEXT fields, not to fixed numbers, so it stays valid when tariffs change.
spending: Spending = purchases - refunds + transfers_to_others; transfers_own are never spending.
'Last month' = the previous full calendar month relative to today, not the current partial month.
'Usual' / 'average monthly' / 'recent' spending = average over the last three full calendar months.
Merchant or category totals are sums of the matching transactions, net of their refunds; check them before confirming a client's figure.
credit: Paying only the minimum avoids late status but NOT interest; only no_interest_payment avoids interest.
due_date, next_cut_off_date, minimum_payment, no_interest_payment, paid_this_period and overdue_days are in the statement: use them, never say they are unknown.
Only use links that exist in the CONTEXT links.
_good_answer_standard: Lead with the direct answer (the number or yes/no), then the breakdown from the client's data, then relevant product conditions and the right app screen link from CONTEXT links.
